transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Um... well, I guess I'm here because I just can't keep my mind on one thing anymore. 

At work... if a saw starts up, or somebody walks past the office, I just lose track. Or even if I just have a thought about another job, it'll pull me off what I’m doing. And then... the whole day just gets away from me.
Did this trouble focusing start recently?

Um... no, I suppose it's been going on for about a year. Maybe a year and a month. It got this bad after I broke my wrist. They had to take me off the hands-on carpentry... shifted me to shop paperwork and supervising instead. It's just been like this since then.
Before you broke your wrist, did you also have trouble paying attention like this?

Well... yeah. I guess it's always been a bit of an issue. Even back in grade school... before I was 12, I think. My teachers were always telling my mother I was... bright, but careless. I was always losing my homework. Or forgetting instructions. I'd just end up staring out the window instead of finishing my seatwork. So... yeah, it's not exactly new.
Did these attention problems also cause trouble for you outside of work, such as at home or in other daily activities?

Yeah... I suppose. 

At home... my husband had to take over paying the bills and keeping track of reminders. I just kept misplacing the papers... or missing things I was supposed to do. 

And it's... well, it's bad at work, too. The mistakes and the delays... it's cost me commissions. I've had to redo jobs. The crew... they don't really want to rely on me for the scheduling or ordering anymore. So... yeah. It affects things.
When you were growing up, did you have trouble understanding social cues or making friends?
No... not really. I had friends. I mean, I wasn't the most popular kid, but... I got along fine. I understood people well enough.
